q.intro.text: Jun and Ava both need the midpoint of segment A B. Jun measures it with a ruler, nine point eight centimeters, and marks four point nine. Ava opens her compass wider than half, swings equal arcs from A and from B, and joins the two crossings. Whose method gives the midpoint exactly, even in principle? Pick one, and say how sure you are.

q.cb.jun.text: You picked Jun’s ruler. A ruler reading is only as good as the reading: nine point eight might be nine point eight one. Ava’s arcs force the midpoint for every segment, and you just proved why.

q.cb.ava.text: You picked Ava’s arcs, and the proof agrees: one compass width, two congruences, and the midpoint and the right angle are forced. No reading involved.

q.cb.same.text: You said both just draw a point. The arcs are not decoration: each one records a distance, and those distances are exactly what the proof used.

e.intro.text: Watch Ava’s construction one step at a time. Each arc is a distance condition; nothing is measured.

e.step0.text: Open the compass wider than half of segment A B, any such width. Needle on A: every point on these arcs is exactly that width, w, from A.

e.step1.text: Keep the width. Needle on B. The crossings P and Q are on both arcs, so they inherit both conditions: P A equals P B equals w, and Q A equals Q B equals w.

e.step2.text: Join P and Q with the straightedge: a line through two points you already have. It crosses segment A B at M.

e.step3.text: M is the midpoint, and line P Q is perpendicular to segment A B: the perpendicular bisector. Both conditions at once. Why they are forced is your job in Prove it.

e.why.text: Why did the compass have to keep the same width from B?

e.why.ok.text: Yes. With one width, each crossing is as far from A as from B. That equality is the whole construction.

e.why.neat.text: Neatness has nothing to do with it. The equal width is what makes P and Q equally far from A and B.

e.why.any.text: Not any arcs: with two different widths, P is farther from one end than the other, and the line misses the midpoint.

t.intro.text: Your turn: bisect the angle at O. Tap the steps in an order that works. One step is not a construction step.

t.decoy.text: That step reads a protractor. A construction never measures: the angle must be halved by arcs alone.

t.early.text: Not yet. That step needs a point or a width that is not on the paper yet.

t.order-done.text: Ray O X is constructed. Now, why does it really bisect the angle?

t.next.text: Why is the angle at O split into two congruent angles?

t.next.ok.text: Yes. O A equals O B from one arc, A X equals B X from the equal arcs, and O X is shared: S S S. Then the angles at O are corresponding parts.

t.next.look.text: Looks are not a reason. Find three pairs of equal sides the compass gave you.

t.next.sas.text: S A S would need the two angles at O to be equal, and that is what you are proving. Use only the sides the compass gave you.

p.intro.text: Back to Ava. Does her construction give the midpoint at a right angle for every segment and every allowed width, or only when it is drawn carefully?

p.build.text: Then prove it. Fill each “because” with the reason that earns the line. Two chips are traps.

p.build-test.text: Let us see what the arcs force, not what a careful drawing shows. Fill each “because” with the reason that earns the line. Two chips are traps.

p.claim1.text: P A equals P B and Q A equals Q B

p.claim2.text: Triangle A P Q is congruent to triangle B P Q, so angle A P M is congruent to angle B P M

p.claim3.text: A M equals B M, and angles A M P and B M P are both ninety degrees

p.c1.text: The arcs about A and B were drawn with one width: P and Q are each equally far from A and B.

p.c2.text: Three pairs of sides: S S S. So the two angles at P match.

p.c3.text: S A S on the two lower triangles: the halves match, and the two angles at M are equal and fill a straight angle. Each is ninety degrees.

p.x-look.text: Looking like the middle is not a reason. Which equal lengths did the compass give you?

p.x-measure.text: A protractor reading checks one drawing. The proof must work for every segment and every width.

p.x-other.text: That reason does not earn this line. What does the line need, and which step gave it?

p.done.text: Proved: for every segment and every width wider than half, line P Q bisects the segment at a right angle. That is why a construction is exact, and a ruler reading is not.
